title: A blocked rebate distribution triggers mandatory public explanation and escalation to Core GovOps
content:
A.6.1.1.7.2.3.2.2.1.2.1.3 continues past the blocking power to define what must happen next: "If Operational GovOps does not execute the distribution, Operational GovOps must post an explanation on the Sky Forum under the 'Osero Prime' category and work with Osero to resolve the disagreement. If Operational GovOps and Osero cannot resolve the disagreement, it must be escalated to Core GovOps."

Three obligations follow automatically from a block, and all are stated as musts. Disclosure is immediate and public, in the same Forum category used for Root Edit proposals, so token holders learn of a withheld distribution without needing to ask. Resolution is collaborative before it is adversarial. And escalation is compulsory — the parties are not permitted to leave the matter unresolved.

The compulsory escalation is the load-bearing part. A blocking veto without a route past it is a deadlock mechanism: whoever holds the veto can extract concessions simply by waiting. Requiring escalation to Core GovOps bounds how long the block can persist and moves the decision to a body with no stake in Osero's specific arithmetic.

This makes the check bidirectional. Operational GovOps can stop Osero from paying out on a bad number, and Osero can force a stubborn or mistaken reviewer to answer to Core GovOps. The forum post ensures both moves happen in the open.
description: Operational GovOps must post its reasoning on the Sky Forum and attempt resolution with Osero; an unresolved disagreement must go up to Core GovOps rather than stalling.
